aiIntegration.learnerResponsibility: Students define the aim, explain the mechanism and plan feedback and adaptation. They develop alternatives, including an approach without AI.
aiIntegration.assessmentFocus: Assess disciplinary fit and a justified change plan (H2). Technical implementation belongs to T3 and ethical deliberation to V1.
aiIntegration.exampleTask: Design two learning-support interventions for a fictional university context, one with and one without AI. Describe mechanisms, possible feedback effects and criteria for later adaptation.

competencies.title: Communicate knowledge clearly
competencies.scope: Present scientific and professional content for its intended audience.
competencies.boundary: Assessment concerns clarity, structure and presentation. Evidential quality belongs to R4; the conversational relationship to K2.

criteria.title: Structure a message for its purpose, audience and format.

opportunities.moduleTitle: Elective seminar: topics in clinical and health psychology
opportunities.text: Structure a bounded disciplinary message for a selected audience.
opportunities.task: Turn the synthesis into a short information resource for a professional audience or fictional advice service.
opportunities.evidence: Information draft with an audience rationale.
opportunities.successCriteria: Structure and terminology suit the audience; limitations remain visible.
opportunities.openDecisions: The seminar leader decides the clinical focus, audience and appropriate proximity to practice.

opportunities.text: Formulate a precise question for scholarly discussion.
opportunities.task: Prepare a short question from the abstract or talk that distinguishes clarification from critical challenge.
opportunities.evidence: Question with an identified reference point.
opportunities.successCriteria: The question is grounded in the talk and allows a substantive response.
opportunities.openDecisions: The actual colloquium determines topic, available materials and discussion format.

opportunities.text: Structure the proposal clearly for scholarly discussion.
opportunities.task: Create a presentation that clearly connects the question, decisive design choice and unresolved need for advice.
opportunities.evidence: Proposal presentation with a focused discussion question.
opportunities.successCriteria: The audience can identify the knowledge claim and contribute to a specific decision.
opportunities.openDecisions: The chair determines presentation time, discussion and whether a revision note is used as learning evidence.

criteria.title: Communicate findings and uncertainty clearly in words or visuals.

opportunities.text: Explain a disciplinary finding to students from another specialisation.
opportunities.task: Create a short figure explanation identifying prerequisite knowledge and uncertainty.
opportunities.evidence: Explanation with audience feedback.
opportunities.successCriteria: The explanation is understandable without losing substantively relevant limitations.
opportunities.openDecisions: The perspectives outlined are examples; the actual offering determines subject matter and collaboration.

opportunities.text: Communicate an uncertain synthesis clearly in a short discussion.
opportunities.task: Present the connection and its weakest point to another person in one minute.
opportunities.evidence: Brief presentation with a question and response.
opportunities.successCriteria: The listener can restate the connection and its limit; brevity does not remove uncertainty.
opportunities.openDecisions: The colloquium determines whether two talks can meaningfully be compared and which discussion format fits.

opportunities.text: Present complex research findings and uncertainty clearly.
opportunities.task: Create a central figure and oral explanation connecting the result, estimation uncertainty and interpretative boundary.
opportunities.evidence: Results presentation with an annotated figure.
opportunities.successCriteria: The presentation shows relevant uncertainty and avoids a stronger claim than the analysis supports.
opportunities.openDecisions: The chair determines format and scope; confidential findings are shown only to an authorised audience.

criteria.title: Revise a presentation in response to specific feedback.

opportunities.moduleTitle: Elective seminar: topics in lifespan developmental psychology
opportunities.text: Revise a developmental argument using specific feedback.
opportunities.task: Revise a paragraph after peer feedback; justify one accepted and one rejected change.
opportunities.evidence: Before-and-after versions with a revision note.
opportunities.successCriteria: The revision improves the disciplinary argument; feedback is not adopted uncritically.
opportunities.openDecisions: The seminar leader selects life stage, topic, readings and suitable evidence; this design requires those choices.

opportunities.text: Improve a scientific argument using specific feedback.
opportunities.task: Revise a central section after supervisory or peer feedback and explain the most important disciplinary changes.
opportunities.evidence: Version comparison with a decision note.
opportunities.successCriteria: The comparison shows changes in reasoning and evidence links, not merely smoother prose.
opportunities.openDecisions: Supervisors must agree the question, search scope, permitted support, evidence format and any assessment adjustment.

opportunities.text: Revise the design using disciplinary critique.
opportunities.task: Seek feedback on a disputed element and document a justified change or retention.
opportunities.evidence: Revision record with a disciplinary rationale.
opportunities.successCriteria: The response addresses the criticism and improves or clarifies the design.
opportunities.openDecisions: The actual seminar offering must be specified. For 505, the inherited module’s own six credits apply, rather than the generic slot’s four credits.

opportunities.text: Revise the proposal selectively after discussion.
opportunities.task: Adopt one justified suggestion and explain why another must be deferred or rejected.
opportunities.evidence: Proposal revision note.
opportunities.successCriteria: Changes are compatible with the independent question; feedback is neither adopted nor rejected wholesale.
opportunities.openDecisions: The chair determines presentation time, discussion and whether a revision note is used as learning evidence.

opportunities.text: Improve the presentation of results following the colloquium.
opportunities.task: Revise a confusing figure or discussion passage using a specific question.
opportunities.evidence: Revised extract with a rationale for the change.
opportunities.successCriteria: The new version resolves the identified comprehension problem and retains disciplinary limits.
opportunities.openDecisions: The chair determines format and scope; confidential findings are shown only to an authorised audience.

levelDescriptions.description: Summarise a short finding clearly for a specified audience.
Plan and revise a reasoned professional account independently.
Communicate complex or contested issues to different audiences without misleading simplification.

aiIntegration.possibleRole: AI can offer wording, translation and presentation variants. AI use, uncertainty and human responsibility also need to be communicated clearly to different audiences.
aiIntegration.learnerResponsibility: Students decide which presentation serves the audience, check changes in meaning and revise after feedback. They explain limits and responsibilities in their own words.
aiIntegration.assessmentFocus: The focus is clarity, structure and audience-sensitive revision (K1). Source checking belongs to R4; obligations to disclose are assessed under V1.
aiIntegration.exampleTask: Explain a fictional AI-assisted research decision to students and to a specialist team. Compare your own and generated versions; revise them using comprehension questions from both groups.

competencies.title: Conduct professional conversations
competencies.scope: Listen, understand perspectives and establish a workable professional relationship.
competencies.boundary: This covers relationships and conversational practice; assessment conclusions belong to H1 and team organisation to K3.

criteria.title: Clarify concerns and perspectives through open questions and listening.

opportunities.text: Elicit different perspectives openly in a guided conversation exercise.
opportunities.task: Conduct a brief role-play using open questions and summarise each perspective for confirmation.
opportunities.evidence: Observation sheet and confirmed summaries.
opportunities.successCriteria: Questions do not suggest answers; summaries are checked by the respective role.
opportunities.openDecisions: Lecturers clarify role boundaries and offer a written alternative for distressing conversational situations.

criteria.title: Structure the conversation transparently and check shared understanding.

opportunities.text: Structure assessment feedback transparently and check understanding.
opportunities.task: Practise a short feedback conversation with uncertainty, questions and an agreed summary in a role-play.
opportunities.evidence: Conversation observation and confirmed summary.
opportunities.successCriteria: The role can restate purpose and limits in their own words; agreement is not equated with understanding.
opportunities.openDecisions: Lecturers determine case complexity, the role of conversation practice and lawfully usable materials.

criteria.title: Respond professionally to emotions, misunderstandings and relational tensions.

opportunities.text: Respond appropriately to a misunderstanding or tension in professional interaction.
opportunities.task: Discuss a concrete or fictionally reconstructed conversation under supervision and rehearse an alternative response.
opportunities.evidence: Anonymised reflection identifying an observable conversational action.
opportunities.successCriteria: The response clarifies the concern and respects role boundaries; private case information remains protected.
opportunities.openDecisions: Practice or research, specific field, supervision, confidentiality and permitted evidence must be agreed individually.

levelDescriptions.description: Listen, ask follow-up questions and reflect understanding in a role-play.
Conduct a bounded conversation purposefully while attending to the other person’s perspective.
Manage a demanding conversation involving ambivalence or tension and recognise personal limits.

aiIntegration.possibleRole: AI can simulate role-play or alternative conversational turns. Trust, concern and differing attitudes towards AI can themselves become topics of professional conversations.
aiIntegration.learnerResponsibility: Students listen, clarify concerns and respond to ambivalence. They distinguish simulated responses from real human experience and also practise with human partners.
aiIntegration.assessmentFocus: Assess listening, shared understanding and responses to relational tension (K2). A successful chat does not establish general conversational or therapeutic competence.
aiIntegration.exampleTask: Conduct a fictional conversation with someone who distrusts an AI recommendation. Practise follow-up questions in a simulation, then discuss with a peer which perspectives the simulation missed.

competencies.title: Organise collaboration
competencies.scope: Organise shared work through clear roles, agreements and accountable handovers.
competencies.boundary: Also applies to teams using AI tools. Tool operation belongs to T2; ethical limits to delegation belong to V1.

criteria.title: Agree on roles, contributions and responsibilities for a shared goal.

opportunities.text: Agree clear roles and responsibility for trying the design.
opportunities.task: Agree roles for delivery, observation and feedback within the group, including how stop signals are handled.
opportunities.evidence: Role agreement for the simulation.
opportunities.successCriteria: Responsibility is clarified before starting; simulation is not presented as authorised real treatment or research.
opportunities.openDecisions: The seminar leader must specify the disciplinary topic, simulation boundaries and technical support.

opportunities.text: Agree personal tasks and responsibility with the placement supervisor.
opportunities.task: At the start, record which activities you may observe, perform under guidance or must not undertake.
opportunities.evidence: Agreed learning and role contract.
opportunities.successCriteria: The agreement fits the actual practice or research placement and identifies a responsible supervisor.
opportunities.openDecisions: Practice or research, specific field, supervision, confidentiality and permitted evidence must be agreed individually.

criteria.title: Keep progress, decisions and handovers traceable for others.

opportunities.text: Document work steps and handovers within the research team.
opportunities.task: Maintain a shared decision log from pilot testing to reporting, with responsibilities and unresolved issues.
opportunities.evidence: Decision and handover log.
opportunities.successCriteria: Other team members can reconstruct decisions and take over a work step.
opportunities.openDecisions: Supervisors agree the project topic, data permissions, team contributions and which plan changes require justification.

opportunities.text: Hand over a complex design decision in a traceable form.
opportunities.task: Prepare a handover for another group specifying remaining risks, changes and outstanding checks.
opportunities.evidence: Handover dossier with answered questions.
opportunities.successCriteria: The other group can understand the current state and necessary boundaries without hidden supplementary information.
opportunities.openDecisions: The lecturer selects the disruption and checks whether a digital tool fits the topic.

opportunities.text: Record proposal decisions arising from supervision traceably.
opportunities.task: After a meeting, record agreed changes, personal tasks and unresolved decisions.
opportunities.evidence: Short, checked meeting note.
opportunities.successCriteria: Personal interpretation and actual agreements remain distinguishable; automatic recording is not assumed.
opportunities.openDecisions: The chair and supervisor determine the topic, data access and proposal scope.

opportunities.text: Hand over a scholarly question to the supervisor with traceable preparatory work.
opportunities.task: Prepare a short request containing the problem, independent attempt, result and decision sought.
opportunities.evidence: Structured request for advice.
opportunities.successCriteria: The supervisor can provide targeted help; the request does not transfer all responsibility without examination.
opportunities.openDecisions: Supervisors agree consultation points, tools and the boundary between independent work and necessary support.

criteria.title: Include differing perspectives and conflicts in a shared working decision.

opportunities.text: Turn differing team positions into a justified working decision.
opportunities.task: Negotiate a team rule in a role-play involving performance expectations, workload and participation.
opportunities.evidence: Decision with documented disagreement.
opportunities.successCriteria: The decision identifies contributions and remaining objections; agreement is not merely asserted.
opportunities.openDecisions: Lecturers select a recruitment or team case and the corresponding quality criteria.

opportunities.text: Consider differing disciplinary positions in a shared decision.
opportunities.task: Discuss an actual seminar case from two perspectives represented in the course and formulate a shared working decision.
opportunities.evidence: Decision retaining counterarguments.
opportunities.successCriteria: Perspectives are considered substantively; remaining disagreement stays visible.
opportunities.openDecisions: The perspectives outlined are examples; the actual offering determines subject matter and collaboration.

levelDescriptions.description: Fulfil an agreed team role and document the contribution.
Coordinate a group task and address task-related conflict.
Organise interdisciplinary collaboration when responsibilities are unclear and goals compete.

aiIntegration.possibleRole: AI can summarise team contributions or suggest tasks. Its use changes coordination, interdisciplinary communication and handovers between people.
aiIntegration.learnerResponsibility: Students agree human responsibilities, make dependencies visible and address differing views on AI use. Generated suggestions enter shared decisions with their origin made clear.
aiIntegration.assessmentFocus: Assess coordination, handovers and shared decisions (K3). Tool operation belongs to T2, technical interfaces to T3 and permissible delegation to V1.
aiIntegration.exampleTask: Organise a fictional team research project with optional AI assistance. Agree responsibilities and handovers; resolve a disagreement about using an unchecked generated contribution.

competencies.title: Understand AI and digital systems
competencies.scope: Explain how relevant systems work, depend on data and are technically limited.
competencies.boundary: Technical explanation is distinct from checking a specific claim in R4 and normative responsibility in V1.

criteria.title: Explain system components and data flows relevant to an application.

opportunities.text: Describe the data flows of a digital learning aid using an example.
opportunities.task: Map input, processing, storage and output in a simple diagram for a supplied learning aid.
opportunities.evidence: Labelled data-flow diagram.
opportunities.successCriteria: The diagram distinguishes local steps from external transfers and marks unknown storage locations.
opportunities.openDecisions: Student tutors and module leads agree the local use note and permitted tools.

criteria.title: Distinguish training, inference, probabilistic outputs and common error mechanisms.

opportunities.text: Explain why a fluent AI response can be factually wrong.
opportunities.task: Compare a real and an invented reference and explain the error through probabilistic text generation.
opportunities.evidence: Short explanation and marked verification steps.
opportunities.successCriteria: Text prediction is not confused with database retrieval; a plausible reference is actually checked.
opportunities.openDecisions: Student tutors and module leads agree the local use note and permitted tools.

criteria.title: Explain technical suitability and limitations for a particular use.

opportunities.text: Explain the limits of a language model as a model of human cognition.
opportunities.task: Compare a supplied model response with a human finding on a language or reasoning task.
opportunities.evidence: Reasoned analysis of explanatory scope.
opportunities.successCriteria: Similar output is not treated as evidence of the same mechanism; a suitable further test is identified.
opportunities.openDecisions: The module lead selects the task and human comparison data.

opportunities.text: Bound the suitability of a digital or AI-supported method for the research question.
opportunities.task: Compare a technical extension with the non-automated alternative using required data and observable performance.
opportunities.evidence: Suitability decision with required checks.
opportunities.successCriteria: Usefulness is justified through the research question; tool availability does not replace a suitability check.
opportunities.openDecisions: The course selects the method and decides whether an AI component is substantively useful at all.

levelDescriptions.description: Use an example to explain why a plausible AI answer can be wrong.
Compare the technical suitability of two systems for a disciplinary task.
Analyse data flows, dependencies and failure conditions in unfamiliar systems.

aiIntegration.possibleRole: AI is the technical object here: data flows, model behaviour, system limits and dependencies. Multimodal and action-taking systems are examined through stable technical questions.
aiIntegration.learnerResponsibility: Students explain relevant mechanisms and infer suitability and failure conditions. They identify knowledge gaps in systems they cannot inspect.
aiIntegration.assessmentFocus: Assess technical understanding (T1), independently of operating speed. Substantive truth remains R4, operation T2 and system design T3.
aiIntegration.exampleTask: Compare a fictional local text-analysis tool with an external multimodal assistant. Map data flows and explain which inferences their outputs cannot technically support.

competencies.title: Use digital and AI tools purposefully
competencies.scope: Operate existing tools for bounded disciplinary tasks, adapt inputs and keep a traceable technical record.
competencies.boundary: T2 concerns using an existing tool; new workflows and component connections belong to T3. An operation record replaces neither analytic reasoning in R3 nor integrity and disclosure requirements in V1.

criteria.title: Translate a bounded disciplinary task into suitable inputs, prompts or operations.

opportunities.text: Translate an independent learning question into suitable inputs for an existing learning aid.
opportunities.task: For a learning aid, formulate a bounded request containing the topic, independent attempt and desired hint; mark the necessary interactions on a supplied interface.
opportunities.evidence: Input draft with corresponding interface actions.
opportunities.successCriteria: The input fits the independent question and requests usable support; it does not inadvertently request a complete replacement answer.
opportunities.openDecisions: Student tutors and module leads agree the local use note and permitted tools.

criteria.title: Operate an existing tool purposefully and adapt inputs or settings with justification.

opportunities.text: Operate an existing tool under guidance and adjust suitable parameters.
opportunities.task: Use a supplied presentation, collection or simulation template and adjust two existing settings to fit the independent learning design.
opportunities.evidence: Output from the operated template with a justified parameter choice.
opportunities.successCriteria: Settings fit the design and their effects can be explained; this task does not require new components or an independently developed application.
opportunities.openDecisions: The seminar leader must specify the disciplinary topic, simulation boundaries and technical support.

criteria.title: Retain relevant settings, operating steps and outputs so that the tool use can be retraced.

opportunities.text: Save the operating sequence, settings and output of an existing learning template traceably.
opportunities.task: For the operated template, save the tool version, selected settings, interaction sequence and corresponding output in a short technical note.
opportunities.evidence: Use note with settings and saved output.
opportunities.successCriteria: Another person can perform the same operating sequence and identify the corresponding output; the note assesses neither the statistical analysis nor ethical permissibility.
opportunities.openDecisions: The seminar leader must specify the disciplinary topic, simulation boundaries and technical support.

levelDescriptions.description: Complete a supplied disciplinary task with an existing tool and record inputs and output.
Adapt operations and settings independently for a typical disciplinary task and document the use transparently.
Learn to use an unfamiliar tool under changing or ambiguous demands, justify adaptations and recognise operational limits.

aiIntegration.possibleRole: An existing digital or AI tool is used for a bounded disciplinary task: formulate suitable inputs, select functions and preserve outputs technically.
aiIntegration.learnerResponsibility: Students operate the tool deliberately, adapt inputs and retain a traceable operation record. They can switch approach when outputs are unsuitable.
aiIntegration.assessmentFocus: Assess task-to-input translation, purposeful operation and technical recording (T2). Analytic reasoning belongs to R3; developing a new workflow belongs to T3.
aiIntegration.exampleTask: Work on a psychology learning question using an existing, operable local template. Prepared AI outputs can serve as examples within it. Adapt inputs and settings and retain operating instructions with a sample output.

competencies.title: Design systems and workflows
competencies.scope: Design and test digital or AI-assisted workflows with technical components, human decisions and verifiable handovers.
competencies.boundary: The focus is system design, integration and functional testing. Operating an existing tool belongs to T2, team agreements to K3, evidential quality to R4 and ethical acceptability to V1.

criteria.title: Decompose a disciplinary task into testable steps, human decisions and defined interfaces.

opportunities.text: Decompose a statistical analysis into checkable work steps.
opportunities.task: Plan data checks, modelling, diagnostics and reporting as separate steps with clear inputs and outputs.
opportunities.evidence: Workflow plan with checkable interfaces.
opportunities.successCriteria: Each step has a disciplinary check; human decisions are identified before potential automation.
opportunities.openDecisions: The module lead determines which taught model families are used for the extended comparison.

opportunities.text: Decompose a complex work task into controllable steps and handovers.
opportunities.task: For a problematic analysis or writing step, outline independent decisions, possible assistance and required checks.
opportunities.evidence: Workflow sketch with human control points.
opportunities.successCriteria: The decomposition makes errors locatable and leaves disciplinary decisions with an identified person.
opportunities.openDecisions: Supervisors agree consultation points, tools and the boundary between independent work and necessary support.

criteria.title: Connect components into a workflow or prototype with clear input and output conditions.

opportunities.text: Connect existing components into a small interactive learning prototype.
opportunities.task: For the independent cognitive learning, intervention or application design, connect a choice, justified feedback and a manual restart, for example through linked presentation slides.
opportunities.evidence: Runnable small prototype with labelled connections.
opportunities.successCriteria: Connections implement the independent workflow and return control; merely operating an unchanged template is insufficient. Disciplinary effects are judged separately.
opportunities.openDecisions: The lecturer selects the disruption and checks whether a digital tool fits the topic.

criteria.title: Develop and document functional tests, error handling and points for human intervention.

opportunities.text: Check a proposed code section using targeted tests.
opportunities.task: Test independent or supplied AI code using missing data and an intentionally reversed category.
opportunities.evidence: Test cases with expected and observed results.
opportunities.successCriteria: At least one silent error becomes detectable; the correction is tested again.
opportunities.openDecisions: Lecturers specify permitted packages and the technical assessment environment.

opportunities.text: Test the functional limits of a tool in use.
opportunities.task: Test a digital template genuinely suited to the design using invalid inputs and a stopping case.
opportunities.evidence: Test log with points for human intervention.
opportunities.successCriteria: Error cases are detected; a functioning tool is not equated with an effective intervention.
opportunities.openDecisions: The lecturer selects the disruption and checks whether a digital tool fits the topic.

opportunities.text: Systematically examine failure boundaries in an automated methodological component.
opportunities.task: Construct a normal case, a boundary case and a failure case for the processing step actually used.
opportunities.evidence: Test log with a stopping signal and recovery procedure.
opportunities.successCriteria: Expected failures are detected; functional testing and statistical validity are judged separately.
opportunities.openDecisions: The specific method, software and suitable failure cases must be specified after module selection.

levelDescriptions.description: Complete a small structured workflow and test a supplied failure case.
Build a workflow from existing components and evaluate it with justified test cases.
Develop a complex workflow under changing demands with interfaces, failure tests and controllable human intervention.

aiIntegration.possibleRole: AI can be part of a newly designed workflow or assist in prototyping. People determine task decomposition, interfaces and controllable intervention points.
aiIntegration.learnerResponsibility: Students design the structure, connect components and test failures. They can explain when a system must hand over to a person or stop.
aiIntegration.assessmentFocus: Assess design, integration and functional tests (T3). This does not establish ethical acceptability, which belongs to V1.
aiIntegration.exampleTask: Design a small learning prototype with prepared AI responses, human source checking and a stop path. Test missing inputs, conflicting outputs and deliberate human override.

competencies.title: Act ethically and responsibly
competencies.scope: Weigh rights, risks, integrity and defensible limits to action in context.
competencies.boundary: AI ethics is an application of this competence. Fairness is judged normatively here; statistical group differences belong to R2/R3.

criteria.title: Identify affected parties, protected interests and possible short- and long-term social or environmental consequences.

opportunities.moduleTitle: Elective seminar: social, economic, organisational, differential psych.
opportunities.text: Identify affected parties and potential harms of a solution.
opportunities.task: Examine both designs for exclusion, manipulation or unwanted burdens, including any AI component.
opportunities.evidence: Map of affected parties and consequences.
opportunities.successCriteria: The map includes people beyond the client and identifies unknown consequences.
opportunities.openDecisions: The actual seminar must determine the topic, available evidence and prototype format.

criteria.title: Weigh options against professional ethical principles and applicable rules.

opportunities.text: Weigh competing goals in digital workplace monitoring.
opportunities.task: Compare productivity, protected interests and discretion in a fictional system and justify a bounded recommendation.
opportunities.evidence: Deliberation note with a rejected alternative.
opportunities.successCriteria: The note considers affected parties and supplied rules; it does not provide unsupported legal advice.
opportunities.openDecisions: The work setting and suitable technical examples are selected within the module.

opportunities.text: Weigh different parties’ interests in a choice design.
opportunities.task: Examine the independent variants for freedom of choice, clarity and potential misuse and justify a revision.
opportunities.evidence: Justified ethical design revision.
opportunities.successCriteria: The revision rests on identified interests and alternatives; technical or legal permissibility alone is not used as an ethical justification.
opportunities.openDecisions: Lecturers select the game or decision problem and credible human comparison findings.

opportunities.text: Weigh responsibility transparently in a substantively uncertain design.
opportunities.task: Discuss who benefits from proposed prioritisation or automation, who bears disadvantages and which alternative remains defensible.
opportunities.evidence: Deliberation specifying responsibility and a revision condition.
opportunities.successCriteria: The decision considers several interests and states when it must be reconsidered.
opportunities.openDecisions: The specialisation determines the target group and setting; ethical deliberation must use suitable supplied rules.

criteria.title: Address consent, privacy, integrity and limits of personal responsibility in the procedure.

opportunities.text: Apply a traceable rule for AI use in a learning task.
opportunities.task: For a sample task, document purpose, assistance used, verification and the part deliberately completed independently.
opportunities.evidence: Completed use note without personal information.
opportunities.successCriteria: The note describes actual work steps; it does not imply approval by a lecturer.
opportunities.openDecisions: Student tutors and module leads agree the local use note and permitted tools.

opportunities.text: Specify participation, data access and responsibility for a student experiment.
opportunities.task: Check the collection procedure against supplied local requirements and document consent, storage and access.
opportunities.evidence: Reviewed procedure plan without participant data.
opportunities.successCriteria: The plan specifies responsibility and limits; consent is not treated as blanket permission for AI processing.
opportunities.openDecisions: Supervisors agree the project topic, data permissions, team contributions and which plan changes require justification.

opportunities.text: Specify responsibility and data flows in digitally supported assessment.
opportunities.task: Mark access, consent questions and decisions that will not be delegated to a system in the fictional procedure.
opportunities.evidence: Responsibility and data-flow plan.
opportunities.successCriteria: The plan refers to supplied local requirements and identifies human responsibility.
opportunities.openDecisions: Lecturers determine case complexity, the role of conversation practice and lawfully usable materials.

opportunities.text: Respect local responsibilities for data and technical support in the placement.
opportunities.task: Clarify in an actual workflow where data goes and which AI uses are permitted, prohibited or unresolved.
opportunities.evidence: Authorised, abstracted workflow note.
opportunities.successCriteria: The note reflects local rules; uncertainty leads to clarification rather than unauthorised data entry.
opportunities.openDecisions: Practice or research, specific field, supervision, confidentiality and permitted evidence must be agreed individually.

opportunities.text: Specify responsibility for data, contributions and automated steps in the project.
opportunities.task: Document permitted data flows, independent and external contributions and decisions for which you remain responsible despite assistance.
opportunities.evidence: Project-specific responsibility and use documentation.
opportunities.successCriteria: Documentation matches agreed project rules and identifies unresolved questions in time; it does not invent approval.
opportunities.openDecisions: Supervisors determine topic, design, data use, permitted support and evidence. Level III describes demanding tasks and is not recorded as attained merely through submission.

levelDescriptions.description: Identify a privacy or integrity issue in a fictional case and give a justified protective measure.
Weigh ethical options for a typical disciplinary task and justify safeguards.
Document a defensible decision under competing goals and uncertain system effects, including limits and escalation needs.

aiIntegration.possibleRole: AI use changes protected interests, autonomy and the distribution of consequences. Power relations, access, longer-term social effects and resource use also inform deliberation.
aiIntegration.learnerResponsibility: Students weigh benefits and risks from affected people’s perspectives, safeguard consent and integrity and justify limits to delegation. They may also decide against use.
aiIntegration.assessmentFocus: Assess ethical deliberation and defensible conduct (V1). AI ethics I–III revisits the same competence at increasing demands and creates no additional category.
aiIntegration.exampleTask: Decide on a fictional AI learning aid whose benefits and long-term effects are uncertain. Consider students with differing resources, data sharing and access to an alternative; record conditions and reasons to stop.

competencies.title: Regulate learning and professional development
competencies.scope: Develop personal learning and working practices using feedback and concrete evidence.
competencies.boundary: Confidence may be self-reported; it is not a competence score inferred from tasks. Disciplinary correctness is assessed under the relevant criterion; source and evidence appraisal belongs to R4.

criteria.title: Identify personal goals, resources and support needs realistically.

opportunities.text: Determine learning needs realistically in the new area.
opportunities.task: Compare an independent explanation before and after reading and choose one unresolved question for the next session.
opportunities.evidence: Learning-needs note with explanation evidence.
opportunities.successCriteria: Needs are derived from concrete explanatory difficulties, not merely subjective confidence.
opportunities.openDecisions: The specific module title, topics and assessment format are absent at slot level and must be added after selection.

opportunities.text: Identify an unresolved personal learning question from a current talk.
opportunities.task: Identify an unclear term or methodological decision and plan how to clarify it through suitable literature.
opportunities.evidence: Follow-up question with a search route.
opportunities.successCriteria: The question arises from a specific limit in understanding; the search route is realistic.
opportunities.openDecisions: The actual colloquium determines topic, available materials and discussion format.

opportunities.text: Estimate resources and learning needs for the master proposal realistically.
opportunities.task: Examine time, methodological knowledge, data access and supervision for the selected question.
opportunities.evidence: Feasibility note with outstanding dependencies.
opportunities.successCriteria: Uncertain resources remain visible; the plan includes a bounded alternative.
opportunities.openDecisions: The chair and supervisor determine the topic, data access and proposal scope.

criteria.title: Plan and use suitable learning or working strategies.

opportunities.text: Plan and apply a learning strategy for a specific study week.
opportunities.task: Plan two short retrieval exercises for lecture content and carry them out at separate times.
opportunities.evidence: Weekly plan with recorded retrieval attempts.
opportunities.successCriteria: The plan specifies time, content and a checkable action; intended and completed work remain distinguishable.
opportunities.openDecisions: Student tutors and module leads agree the local use note and permitted tools.

opportunities.text: Replan the research process when an unexpected problem occurs.
opportunities.task: Bring an actual or prepared problem and create a bounded next work cycle.
opportunities.evidence: Revised work plan with a decision point.
opportunities.successCriteria: The plan addresses the specific barrier and states a condition for consultation or stopping.
opportunities.openDecisions: Supervisors agree consultation points, tools and the boundary between independent work and necessary support.

criteria.title: Review and adapt personal learning and self-regulation using feedback and performance situations, including when tools could displace personal reasoning.

opportunities.text: Use errors in an independent case response to improve the next task.
opportunities.task: Compare the first response with feedback and record which reasoning step you will change in the next vignette.
opportunities.evidence: Error and transfer note.
opportunities.successCriteria: The note identifies a specific reasoning error and observable next step; a better AI response is not counted as independent learning evidence.
opportunities.openDecisions: The module lead decides which feedback is automated and which is provided by qualified supervision.

opportunities.text: Examine independent reasoning when using delegated support and adapt the approach.
opportunities.task: Explain a central conclusion without aids; compare this with your work log and adapt a task that was delegated too extensively.
opportunities.evidence: Reflection note with a concrete change to working practice.
opportunities.successCriteria: The note draws on an independent explanation attempt and distinguishes text quality from personal understanding.
opportunities.openDecisions: Supervisors must agree the question, search scope, permitted support, evidence format and any assessment adjustment.

opportunities.text: Adapt working strategy based on the design process.
opportunities.task: Use an independent explanation of the product to examine which steps you understood and which you delegated too early.
opportunities.evidence: Strategy adjustment with a checkable next attempt.
opportunities.successCriteria: Reflection leads to a concrete change; product success is not equated with personal competence attainment.
opportunities.openDecisions: The actual seminar offering must be specified. For 505, the inherited module’s own six credits apply, rather than the generic slot’s four credits.

opportunities.text: Adapt personal working practices using supervised feedback.
opportunities.task: Compare an agreed learning goal with an observed activity and plan a concrete next practice opportunity.
opportunities.evidence: Reflection section with a supervised next task.
opportunities.successCriteria: The conclusion draws on activity and feedback; attendance hours alone are not treated as competence evidence.
opportunities.openDecisions: Practice or research, specific field, supervision, confidentiality and permitted evidence must be agreed individually.

opportunities.text: Revise working practices under uncertainty and AI offloading using performance evidence.
opportunities.task: Explain a central analysis without assistance, examine a gap in understanding and adapt the next work cycle accordingly.
opportunities.evidence: Justified strategy change with a further explanation attempt.
opportunities.successCriteria: The change strengthens a specified independent reasoning process; completed text or code alone does not establish understanding.
opportunities.openDecisions: Supervisors determine topic, design, data use, permitted support and evidence. Level III describes demanding tasks and is not recorded as attained merely through submission.

opportunities.text: Adapt examination preparation based on independent explanation attempts.
opportunities.task: Give two practice answers at separate times and examine whether feedback or optional AI assistance improved independent explanation.
opportunities.evidence: Comparison of practice answers with the next learning step.
opportunities.successCriteria: Adaptation follows concrete errors; familiarity with a model answer is insufficient as learning evidence.
opportunities.openDecisions: Examiners agree the actual reading, scope and applicable examination conditions.

levelDescriptions.description: Carry out a small learning plan and explain a useful adjustment.
Adapt personal learning independently in response to specific difficulties.
Manage personal development in open, sustained tasks and seek targeted support when needed.

aiIntegration.possibleRole: AI can support feedback, practice variation and learning plans. It may also displace personal reasoning or create an unwarranted sense of understanding.
aiIntegration.learnerResponsibility: Students set their own goals, choose support and check understanding without AI as well. They adapt strategies to actual difficulties and seek help when needed.
aiIntegration.assessmentFocus: Assess reasoned self-regulation using learning evidence (V2). Confidence remains self-report; disciplinary correctness is assessed under the relevant criterion.
aiIntegration.exampleTask: Attempt a task independently, then use prepared AI feedback and later attempt an unaided transfer task. Compare expected and demonstrated understanding and justify changes to your learning plan.
